topic: DeepSeek launches open-source Super-Agent AI coding agent
headline_marked: [[DeepSeek launches "Super-Agent"]], an open-source AI coding agent to rival Claude Code
headline: DeepSeek launches "Super-Agent", an open-source AI coding agent to rival Claude Code
summary: DeepSeek's new open-source AI coding agent, "Super-Agent," is designed to autonomously handle software development tasks, challenging tools like Anthropic's Claude Code. It's released on GitHub under the MIT license.
details: DeepSeek has released "Super-Agent," an open-source AI coding agent under the MIT license on GitHub. This new tool is positioned as a direct competitor to established solutions like Anthropic's Claude Code, aiming to enhance software development efficiency. It's available at github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype.

The Super-Agent architecture features a novel two-layer "Router & Worker" system. This design moves beyond traditional single-session AI coding tools, which often demand constant human oversight and prompt management. The goal is to reduce human attention limits in the development process.

topic: Mistral Large 4 open weights released for local deployment
headline_marked: [[Mistral Large 4 open weights]] released, 1.05T params available for self-hosting
headline: Mistral Large 4 open weights released, 1.05T params available for self-hosting
summary: Mistral's flagship 1.05T parameter multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model, "Le Chonk," is now downloadable under an MIT-modified license, offering the same power as its API.
details: Mistral has officially released the open weights for its flagship Large 4 model, codenamed "Le Chonk," on Hugging Face. This 1.05T parameter multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model is identical to the version offered via Mistral's API. It's available under an MIT-modified license.

The model features approximately 49B active parameters per token (52B including embeddings and output layers), a 1.6B vision encoder, and a substantial 1M token context window. Downloads are available in FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints, with community-contributed GGUF quants also accessible.

This release is an updated version compared to the October 6 preview. Mistral states the model underwent an additional three weeks of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), with a specific focus on enhancing coding capabilities and cybersecurity safety.

Mistral reports strong benchmark results, including 19.7% on Cognition's private FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, marking the highest open-weight score on their chart. It also achieved 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, nearing GLM-5.3's performance.

For self-hosting, the model is designed to run efficiently on a single node with 8 data center GPUs, utilizing frameworks like vLLM or SGLang. Official serving examples assume 8-way tensor parallelism for optimal performance.

The FP8 download alone takes over two hours at a continuous 1 Gbps connection. For Apple Silicon users, the Q2_K GGUF quant (381 GB) can fit on an M3 Ultra with 512 GB unified memory, offering around 15 tokens/second generation speed.

Developers integrating the model should note a change in reasoning mode; if using reasoning_effort: "none" from the preview, it should be updated to "low" to avoid token wastage. Proper parser flags are crucial to prevent reasoning leakage into content.

For those preferring not to manage hardware, Mistral Large 4 remains accessible via the Mistral API at $0.70 per million input tokens. Both self-hosted vLLM/SGLang servers and the official API are OpenAI-compatible.
